text:
|Time|Ready queue|Analysis|
|--|--|--|
|0|**P1(5)**|Only P1 has arrived in the ready queue, so P1 is put on the processor to run for one time slice|
|2|**P2(4)**->P1(3)|P2 arrives in the ready queue; P1 has finished one time slice and is deprived of the processor and placed back at the tail of the queue. At this time P2 is at the head of the queue, so P2 is put on the processor. (Note: at time 2, P1 leaves the processor, and at the same moment the new process P2 arrives; **by default, newly arrived processes enter the ready queue first**)|
|4|**P1(3)**->P3(1)->P2(2)|P3 arrives and is first inserted at the tail of the ready queue; immediately afterward, P2 leaves the processor and is also inserted at the tail of the queue|
|5|P3(1)->P2(2)->P4(6)|P4 arrives and is inserted at the tail of the ready queue. Since P1's time slice has not yet been used up, no scheduling occurs for the moment. In addition, P1 is currently in the running state and is not in the ready queue|
|6|**P3(1)**->P2(2)->P4(6)->P1(1)|P1's time slice is used up, so it leaves the processor and is placed back at the tail of the ready queue; scheduling occurs|
|7|**P2(2)**->P4(6)->P1(1)|Although P3's time slice is not used up, P3 only needs to run for 1 unit of time. After finishing, it **voluntarily gives up the processor**, so scheduling also occurs. The process at the head of the queue, P2, is put on the processor.|
|9|**P4(6)**->P1(1)|Process P2's time slice is used up and it happens to finish running; scheduling occurs, and P4 is put on the processor|
|11|**P1(1)**->P4(4)|P4's time slice is used up and it returns to the ready queue. P1 is put on the processor|
|12|**P4(4)**|P1 finishes running and voluntarily gives up the processor; at this time only P4 remains in the ready queue, so P4 is put on the processor|
|14|-|The ready queue is empty, so P4 continues to run for one more time slice|
